clinician.final_diagnosis: pubic symphysis disjunction syndrome following a dystocic delivery
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old primigravida presented on postpartum day 1 with acute pubic pain and increased abdomino-pelvic sensitivity to palpation of the pubic symphysis following delivery of a large infant (4400g) at a peripheral hospital. Imaging workup confirmed the diagnosis: pelvic X-ray demonstrated pubic disjunction, and abdomino-pelvic CT revealed a 3 cm pubic symphysis disjunction with soft tissue infiltration but no fracture or collection. The sacroiliac and coxo-femoral joints were normal. Conservative management was initiated with unloading, preventive anticoagulation, and analgesic treatment (paracetamol and NSAIDs). Clinical evolution was favorable with resolution of symptoms; follow-up examination at 15 days post-admission showed no symphysial tenderness and absence of painful recurrence.
